models, viewpoints, and tools used by the practitioner.
blocks.text_zh: 其次确定如何处理这些特征。通常不应大改框架，而应调整模型、视点及工具。

blocks.text_en:
In Phase B, Phase C, and Phase D the practitioner is expected to select
the relevant architecture resources, including models, viewpoints, and
tools, to properly describe the architecture domain and demonstrate that
stakeholder concerns are addressed (see the TOGAF Standard — ADM Techniques ).
Depending upon the distinctive features, different architectural styles will add new elements that must be described, highlight existing elements, adjust the notation used to describe the architecture, and
focus the architect on some stakeholders or stakeholder concerns.
blocks.text_zh: B、C、D中应选择相关模型、视点和工具描述域并证明关注点被处理。不同风格可增加需描述要素、突出已有要素、调整记法、聚焦特定利益相关者或关注点。

blocks.text_en:
Addressing the distinctive features will usually include extensions to
the Architecture Content Metamodel and the use of specific notation or
modeling techniques and the identification of viewpoints. Dominance of a particular architectural style can direct the practitioner to revisit the Preliminary Phase to make changes to the Architecture Capability or to address a distinctive feature in the expected scope of a single ADM
cycle.
blocks.text_zh: 通常包括内容元模型扩展、特定记法或技术及视点识别。主导风格可能使实践者重访预备阶段调整能力，或在单周期预期范围内处理独特特征。

blocks.text_en:
Style-specific reference models and maturity models are commonly used
tools that support a practitioner.
blocks.text_zh: 风格特定参考模型和成熟度模型是常用工具。

blocks.text_en:
During the lifetime of the TOGAF framework many architectural styles
have been developed to address key problems facing practitioners and to
demonstrate how the TOGAF framework can be made more relevant within
defined contexts.
blocks.text_zh: TOGAF发展中出现多种风格，以处理实践关键问题并提高特定语境相关性。

blocks.text_en: Some of these have been developed by The Open Group Forums and Work Groups working in specific areas and have been published in Guides, White Papers, and Standards. Examples include:
blocks.text_zh: 部分由The Open Group论坛和工作组开发，以指南、白皮书或标准发布，例如：

blocks.text_en: TOGAF ® Series Guide: Using the TOGAF ® Framework to Define and Govern Service-Oriented Architectures TOGAF ® Series Guide: Integrating Risk and Security within a TOGAF ® Enterprise Architecture
blocks.text_zh:
- 《使用TOGAF定义和治理面向服务架构》。
- 《在TOGAF企业架构中集成风险与安全》。

blocks.text_en: Some of these have been developed collaboratively between The Open Group and other bodies. Examples include:
blocks.text_zh: 部分与其他机构协作，例如：

blocks.text_en: TOGAF ® and SABSA ® Integration Archi Banking Group: Combining the BIAN Reference Model, ArchiMate ® Modeling Notation, and the TOGAF ® Framework Exploring Synergies between TOGAF ® and Frameworx TOGAF ® 9 and DoDAF 2.0
blocks.text_zh:
- TOGAF与SABSA集成。
- Archi Banking：结合BIAN参考模型、ArchiMate记法及TOGAF。
- 探索TOGAF与Frameworx协同。
- TOGAF 9与DoDAF 2.0。

blocks.text_en:
The TOGAF Library (see www.opengroup.org/togaf-library )
is a structured library of resources that support the TOGAF Standard.
blocks.text_zh: TOGAF资料库www.opengroup.org/togaf-library提供支持标准的结构化资源。

blocks.text_en: 3.16. Architecture Views and Viewpoints
blocks.text_zh: 3.16. 架构视图与视点

blocks.text_en:
The ability to create specific “views” of parts of a complex architecture is fundamental in being able to communicate with and allay concerns of stakeholders or groups of stakeholders. To gain full understanding and support from stakeholders it is necessary to present
information in a form that each stakeholder will relate to and understand.
blocks.text_zh: 创建复杂架构局部特定视图，是沟通并处理利益相关者关注点的基础。获得充分理解和支持，需以各方能联系并理解的形式呈现信息。

blocks.text_en: The role of architecture views is shown in Figure 3-10 , adapted from more formal definitions contained in ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2015.
blocks.text_zh: 视图作用见图3-10，改编自ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022及15288:2015更正式定义。
原图：Basic Architectural Concepts

blocks.text_en: Figure 3-10: Basic Architectural Concepts
blocks.text_zh: 图3-10：基本架构概念

blocks.text_en: 3.17. Enterprise Agility
blocks.text_zh: 3.17. 企业敏捷性

blocks.text_en:
Enterprise agility is a commonly used term, but the exact definition
differs among practitioners. Regardless of how the term is defined, it
is important because it enables an enterprise to better react to change by being more customer and product-centric, more efficient, and better
able to ensure regulatory compliance.
blocks.text_zh: 实践者定义有所不同，但它使企业更以客户和产品为中心、更有效率、更能确保法规遵从，从而更好响应变化。

blocks.text_en:
The term “Agile” is frequently associated with Agile software
development processes associated with the Manifesto for Agile Software
Development.
blocks.text_zh: Agile常与敏捷软件开发宣言相关流程相联系。

blocks.text_en:
While these “Agile” principles and techniques can be applied to adapt
the TOGAF framework, enterprise agility is a broader context than Agile software development. Therefore, additional techniques are employed in
adapting the TOGAF framework to an Agile enterprise.
blocks.text_zh: 敏捷原则和技术可用于适配TOGAF，但企业敏捷范围更广，需额外技术。

blocks.text_en:
Enterprise Architecture provides a framework for change, linked to both strategic direction and business value. It provides a sufficient view of
the organization to manage complexity, support continuous change, and manage the risk of unanticipated consequences.
blocks.text_zh: EA将变革与战略方向、业务价值关联，提供足够组织视图来管理复杂性、持续变革和意外后果风险。

blocks.text_en: The TOGAF framework has embraced the call to respond to the needs of the enterprise in a timely manner, through the concepts of “partitions” and “levels”. Partitions define how the work is broken down into multiple architecture initiatives. Levels define how the overall architecture can be developed at different levels of granularity and detail.
blocks.text_zh: TOGAF以分区和层级及时响应企业需要：分区将工作分成多个架构举措；层级支持不同粒度和详细程度开发。

blocks.text_en:
In addition, the TOGAF ADM supports a number of concepts that are
characterized as iteration.
blocks.text_zh: ADM还支持多个迭代概念。

blocks.text_en:
More detailed descriptions of how to adapt the TOGAF ADM to support
enterprise agility can be found in:
blocks.text_zh: 详细适配描述见：

blocks.text_en: TOGAF ® Series Guide: Applying the TOGAF ® ADM using Agile Sprints TOGAF ® Series Guide: Enabling Enterprise Agility The Open Agile Architecture™ Standard
blocks.text_zh:
- 《使用敏捷Sprint应用TOGAF ADM》。
- 《使能企业敏捷性》。
- 《开放敏捷架构标准》。

blocks.text_en: 3.18. Risk Management
blocks.text_zh: 3.18. 风险管理

blocks.text_en: There will always be risk with any architecture/business transformation effort. It is important to identify, classify, and mitigate these risks before starting so that they can be tracked throughout the transformation effort.
blocks.text_zh: 任何架构/业务转型都有风险；应事先识别、分类、缓解，并全程跟踪。

blocks.text_en:
Mitigation is an ongoing effort and often the risk triggers may be
outside the scope of the transformation planners (e.g., merger,
acquisition) so planners must monitor the transformation context
constantly.
blocks.text_zh: 缓解持续进行。并购等风险触发因素可能超出规划者范围，因此必须持续监控语境。

blocks.text_en:
It is also important to note that the Enterprise Architect may identify
the risks and mitigate certain ones, but it is within the governance
framework that risks have to be first accepted and then managed.
blocks.text_zh: 架构师可识别并缓解部分风险，但风险必须在治理框架内先接受、后管理。

blocks.text_en: There are two levels of risk that should be considered, namely:
blocks.text_zh: 应考虑两级风险：

blocks.text_en:
Initial level of risk: risk categorization prior to determining and
implementing mitigating actions Residual level of risk: risk categorization after implementation of
mitigating actions (if any)
blocks.text_zh:
- 初始风险：确定和实施缓解行动前的分类。
- 剩余风险：实施缓解行动（若有）后的分类。

blocks.text_en: The process for risk management consists of the following activities:
blocks.text_zh: 过程包括：

blocks.text_en: Risk classification Risk identification Initial risk assessment Risk mitigation and residual risk assessment Risk monitoring
blocks.text_zh: - 分类、识别、初始评估、缓解及剩余风险评估、监控。

blocks.text_en: A qualitative approach to risk management is described in the TOGAF Standard — ADM Techniques .
blocks.text_zh: 定性方法见《ADM技术》。

blocks.text_en:
Risk concepts are included in the Enterprise Security Architecture
described in the
blocks.text_zh: 企业安全架构中的风险概念见：

blocks.text_en: TOGAF ® Series Guide: Integrating Risk and Security within a TOGAF ® Enterprise Architecture
blocks.text_zh: - 《在TOGAF企业架构中集成风险与安全》。

blocks.text_en:
A more rigorous quantitative approach is described in the Open
FAIR™ Body of Knowledge which comprises two standards from The Open
Group: Open Risk Taxonomy (O-RT) and Open Risk Analysis (O-RA).
blocks.text_zh: 更严格的定量方法见Open FAIR知识体系，包含开放风险分类法O-RT和开放风险分析O-RA两项标准。

blocks.text_en: 4. Definitions
blocks.text_zh: 4. 定义

blocks.text_en:
For the purposes of the TOGAF Standard, the following terms and
definitions apply. Appendix B, Glossary of Supplementary Definitions should be referenced for supplementary definitions not
defined in this chapter. The Merriam-Webster ® Collegiate Dictionary
should be referenced for terms not defined in this section or Appendix B, Glossary of Supplementary Definitions .
blocks.text_zh: 下列术语定义适用于本标准。补充定义见附录B；两处均未定义的术语参照Merriam-Webster Collegiate Dictionary。

blocks.text_en: 4.1. Abstraction

The technique of providing summarized or generalized descriptions of
detailed and complex content.
blocks.text_zh: 对详细复杂内容提供摘要或一般化描述的技术。

blocks.text_en:
Note: Abstraction, as in “level of abstraction”, can also mean providing a
focus for analysis that is concerned with a consistent and common
level of detail or abstraction. Abstraction in this sense is typically
used in architecture to allow a consistent level of definition and
understanding to be achieved in each area of the architecture in order
to support effective communication and decision-making. It is
especially useful when dealing with large and complex architectures as
it allows relevant issues to be identified before further detail is
attempted.
blocks.text_zh: 注：“抽象层次”也可指为分析聚焦一致、共同的细节或抽象程度。在架构各领域达成一致定义和理解，支持有效沟通决策；尤其有助在复杂大型架构深入细节前识别相关问题。

blocks.text_en: 4.2. Actor
blocks.text_zh: 4.2. 参与者

blocks.text_en:
A person, organization, or system that has one or more roles that
initiates or interacts with activities; for example, a sales
representative who travels to visit customers. Actors may be internal or
external to an organization.
blocks.text_zh: 具有一个或多个角色、发起或参与活动的人、组织或系统，如外出访客的销售代表，可为组织内部或外部。

blocks.text_en:
Note: In the automotive industry, an original equipment manufacturer would
be considered an actor by an automotive dealership that interacts with
its supply chain activities.
blocks.text_zh: 注：汽车经销商可将参与供应链活动的原始设备制造商视为参与者。

blocks.text_en: 4.3. Application Architecture
blocks.text_zh: 4.3. 应用架构

blocks.text_en:
A description of the structure and interaction of the applications that
provide key business capabilities and manage the data assets.
blocks.text_zh: 描述提供关键业务能力、管理数据资产的应用结构及交互。

blocks.text_en: Note: Application Architecture is described in the TOGAF Standard — Architecture Development Method .
blocks.text_zh: 注：应用架构见《架构开发方法》。

blocks.text_en: 4.4. Application Component
blocks.text_zh: 4.4. 应用组件

blocks.text_en:
An encapsulation of application functionality aligned to implementation
structure, which is modular and replaceable. It encapsulates its
behavior and data, provides services, and makes them available through
interfaces.
blocks.text_zh: 与实现结构对齐、模块化且可替换的应用功能封装；封装行为和数据，提供服务并通过接口开放。

blocks.text_en:
Note: For example, a business application such as an accounting, payroll, or
CRM system. An application component usually maintains a data component. It is
enabled by technology services provided by technology components.
blocks.text_zh: 注：如会计、薪资、CRM系统；通常维护数据组件，由技术组件提供的技术服务使能。

blocks.text_en: 4.5. Application Platform
blocks.text_zh: 4.5. 应用平台

blocks.text_en:
The collection of technology components of hardware and software that
provide the services used to support applications.
blocks.text_zh: 提供应用支撑服务的软硬件技术组件集合。

blocks.text_en: 4.6. Application Service
blocks.text_zh: 4.6. 应用服务

blocks.text_en:
A discrete behavior requestable from an application; an automated
element supporting or delivering part or all of one or more business
services.
blocks.text_zh: 可向应用请求的独立行为；支持或交付一个或多个业务服务部分或全部的自动化要素。

blocks.text_en: 4.7. Architectural Style
blocks.text_zh: 4.7. 架构风格

blocks.text_en:
The combination of distinctive features related to the specific context
within which architecture is performed or expressed; a collection of
principles and characteristics that steer or constrain how an
architecture is formed.
blocks.text_zh: 与架构执行或表达的特定语境有关的独特特征组合；引导或约束架构形成的原则和特征集合。

blocks.text_en: 4.8. Architecture

The fundamental concepts or properties of an entity in its environment
and governing principles for the realization and evolution of this entity and its related lifecycle processes
(Source: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022) The structure of components, their inter-relationships, and the
principles and guidelines governing their design and evolution over
time
blocks.text_zh:
1. 实体在环境中的基本概念或属性，以及支配其实现、演进和相关生命周期流程的原则（ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022）。
2. 组件结构、相互关系及支配其随时间设计演进的原则和指导。

blocks.text_en: 4.9. Architecture Building Block (ABB)
blocks.text_zh: 4.9. 架构构建块ABB

blocks.text_en:
An architectural component that specifies the required Solution Building
Blocks (SBBs) at a more logical (or supplier-independent) level.
blocks.text_zh: 以更逻辑化或供应商无关层次规定所需SBB的架构组件。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.26, “Building Block” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.26构建块。

blocks.text_en: 4.10. Architecture Continuum
blocks.text_zh: 4.10. 架构连续系列

blocks.text_en:
A categorization mechanism, with increasing detail and specialization,
for the components and artifacts stored in the Architecture Landscape or
Reference Library (part of the Architecture Repository).
blocks.text_zh: 按不断增加的详细程度及特化程度，对架构全景或参考库（储存库的一部分）的组件和制品分类的机制。

blocks.text_en:
Note: This Continuum begins with foundational definitions like reference
models, core strategies, and basic building blocks. From there it
spans to Industry Architectures and all the way to an
Organization-Specific Architecture.
blocks.text_zh: 注：始于参考模型、核心战略和基本块等基础定义，延伸至行业架构和组织特定架构。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.45, “Enterprise Continuum” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.45企业连续系列。

blocks.text_en: 4.11. Architecture Development Method (ADM)
blocks.text_zh: 4.11. 架构开发方法ADM

blocks.text_en:
The core of the TOGAF framework. A multi-phase, iterative approach to
develop and use an Enterprise Architecture to shape and govern business
transformation.
blocks.text_zh: TOGAF核心，以多阶段迭代方式开发、使用EA，塑造并治理业务转型。

blocks.text_en: Note: The ADM is described in the TOGAF Standard — ADM Techniques .
blocks.text_zh: 注：本地原文指向《ADM技术》。

blocks.text_en: 4.12. Architecture Domain

The architectural area being considered. The TOGAF framework follows the
tradition of dividing Enterprise Architecture into four primary
architecture domains: business, data, application, and technology. Other
domains (motivation, security, governance, etc.) may span those four
primary domains.
blocks.text_zh: 所考虑的架构领域。TOGAF传统分业务、数据、应用、技术四主域；动机、安全、治理等可跨四域。

blocks.text_en: 4.13. Architecture Framework
blocks.text_zh: 4.13. 架构框架

blocks.text_en:
A conceptual structure used to plan, develop, implement, govern, and
sustain an architecture.
blocks.text_zh: 用于规划、开发、实施、治理和持续维护架构的概念结构。

blocks.text_en: 4.14. Architecture Governance
blocks.text_zh: 4.14. 架构治理

blocks.text_en:
The practice of monitoring and directing architecture-related work. The
goal is to deliver desired outcomes and adhere to relevant principles,
standards, and roadmaps.
blocks.text_zh: 监控和指导架构相关工作的实践，目标是交付期望结果，遵循相关原则、标准及路线图。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.49, “Governance” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.49治理。

blocks.text_en: 4.15. Architecture Landscape
blocks.text_zh: 4.15. 架构全景

blocks.text_en: The architectural representation of assets in use, or planned, by the enterprise at particular points in time.
blocks.text_zh: 企业在特定时点在用或计划资产的架构表示。

blocks.text_en: 4.16. Architecture Level
blocks.text_zh: 4.16. 架构层级

blocks.text_en:
Levels provide a framework for dividing the Architecture Landscape into
levels of granularity.
blocks.text_zh: 将架构全景按粒度层次划分的框架。

blocks.text_en: Note: Architecture levels are distinct from architecture partitions.
blocks.text_zh: 注：架构层级与架构分区不同。

blocks.text_en: 4.17. Architecture Model
blocks.text_zh: 4.17. 架构模型

blocks.text_en: A representation of a subject of interest.
blocks.text_zh: 对关注对象的表示。

blocks.text_en:
Note: An architecture model provides a smaller scale, simplified, and/or
abstract representation of the subject matter.
blocks.text_zh: 注：提供较小尺度、简化和/或抽象表示。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.76, “Stakeholder” , Section 4.20, “Architecture View” , and Section 4.21, “Architecture Viewpoint” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.76利益相关者、4.20视图、4.21视点。

blocks.text_en: 4.18. Architecture Partition
blocks.text_zh: 4.18. 架构分区

blocks.text_en:
A subset of architecture resulting from dividing that architecture to
facilitate its development and management.
blocks.text_zh: 为方便开发和管理而分割架构得到的子集。

blocks.text_en: 4.19. Architecture Principle
blocks.text_zh: 4.19. 架构原则

blocks.text_en:
A qualitative statement of intent that should be met by the
architecture.
blocks.text_zh: 架构应满足的定性意图陈述。

blocks.text_en: Note: A sample set of Architecture Principles is defined in the TOGAF Standard — ADM Techniques .
blocks.text_zh: 注：原则示例集见《ADM技术》。

blocks.text_en: 4.20. Architecture View
blocks.text_zh: 4.20. 架构视图

blocks.text_en: A representation of a system from the perspective of a related set of concerns.
blocks.text_zh: 从一组相关关注点视角表示系统。

blocks.text_en:
Note: In some sections of this standard, the term “view” is used as a
synonym for “architecture view”.
blocks.text_zh: 注：部分章节以view作为architecture view同义词。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.76, “Stakeholder” and Section 4.21, “Architecture Viewpoint” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.76利益相关者和4.21视点。

blocks.text_en: 4.21. Architecture Viewpoint
blocks.text_zh: 4.21. 架构视点

blocks.text_en:
A specification of the conventions for a particular kind of architecture
view.
blocks.text_zh: 规定某类架构视图约定的规格。

blocks.text_en:
Note: An architecture viewpoint can also be seen as the definition or schema
for that kind of architecture view. It establishes the conventions for constructing, interpreting, and using an architecture view to address
a specific concern (or set of concerns) about a system-of-interest. In some sections of this standard, the term “viewpoint” is used as a
synonym for “architecture viewpoint”.
blocks.text_zh: 注：也可看作该类视图定义或模式，规定构建、解释、使用视图以处理关注系统特定关注点集合的约定。部分章节用viewpoint作同义词。

blocks.text_en: See also Section B.25, “Metaview” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见B.25元视图。

blocks.text_en: 4.22. Architecture Vision
blocks.text_zh: 4.22. 架构愿景

blocks.text_en: A succinct description of the Target Architecture that describes its business value and the changes to the enterprise that will result from its successful deployment. It serves as an aspirational vision and a boundary for detailed architecture development.
blocks.text_zh: 简洁描述目标架构、业务价值及成功部署对企业的变化；作为期望愿景和详细开发边界。

blocks.text_en: Note: Phase A (Architecture Vision) is described in the TOGAF Standard — Architecture Development Method .
blocks.text_zh: 注：A阶段见《架构开发方法》。

blocks.text_en: 4.23. Artifact

An architectural work product that describes an aspect of the
architecture.
blocks.text_zh: 描述架构某方面的工作产品。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.26, “Building Block” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.26构建块。

blocks.text_en: 4.24. Baseline

A specification that has been formally reviewed and agreed upon, that
thereafter serves as the basis for further development or change and
that can be changed only through formal change control procedures or a
type of procedure such as configuration management.
blocks.text_zh: 已正式评审商定的规格，作为后续开发或变更基础，只能通过正式变更控制或配置管理等程序改变。

blocks.text_en: 4.25. Boundaryless Information Flow™
blocks.text_zh: 4.25. 无边界信息流

blocks.text_en:
A shorthand representation of “access to integrated information to
support business process improvements” representing a desired state of
an enterprise’s infrastructure specific to the business needs of the
organization.
blocks.text_zh: “访问集成信息以支持业务流程改进”的简称，代表符合组织业务需要的基础设施期望状态。

blocks.text_en: Note: The need for Boundaryless Information Flow, a trademark of The Open Group, is described in the TOGAF ® Series Guide: The TOGAF Integrated Information Infrastructure Reference Model (III-RM) .
blocks.text_zh: 注：无边界信息流是The Open Group商标，相关需要见III-RM系列指南。

blocks.text_en: 4.26. Building Block

A potentially re-usable component that can be combined with other
building blocks to deliver architectures and solutions.
blocks.text_zh: 可潜在复用的组件，与其他构建块组合交付架构和方案。

blocks.text_en:
Note: Building blocks can be defined at various levels of detail, depending
  on what stage of architecture development has been reached. E.g., at an early stage, a building block can simply consist of a name or an outline description. Later on, a building block may be
  decomposed into multiple supporting building blocks and may be accompanied by a full specification. Building blocks can relate to “architectures” or “solutions”. They are described in the TOGAF Standard — Architecture Content . See also Section 4.23, “Artifact” .
blocks.text_zh: 注：详细程度依阶段而异，早期可为名称概要，后续可分解并附完整规格；可属于架构或方案。见《架构内容》及4.23制品。

blocks.text_en: 4.27. Business Architecture
blocks.text_zh: 4.27. 业务架构

blocks.text_en:
A representation of holistic, multi-dimensional business views of:
capabilities, end-to-end value delivery, information, and organizational
structure; and the relationships among these business views and
strategies, products, policies, processes, initiatives, and
stakeholders.
blocks.text_zh: 能力、端到端价值交付、信息和组织结构的整体多维业务视图，以及这些视图同战略、产品、政策、流程、举措、利益相关者关系的表示。

blocks.text_en:
Note: Business Architecture relates business elements to business goals and
elements of other domains. Business Architecture is described in the TOGAF Standard — Architecture Development Method .
blocks.text_zh: 注：将业务要素关联到业务目标及其他域要素，见《架构开发方法》。

blocks.text_en: 4.28. Business Capability
blocks.text_zh: 4.28. 业务能力

blocks.text_en:
A particular ability that a business may possess or exchange to achieve
a specific purpose.
blocks.text_zh: 业务为实现特定目的可能拥有或交换的特定能力。

blocks.text_en: 4.29. Business Function
blocks.text_zh: 4.29. 业务职能

blocks.text_en: A collection of business behavior based on a chosen set of criteria, closely aligned to an organization.
blocks.text_zh: 按所选准则形成、紧密对应组织的业务行为集合。

blocks.text_en: 4.30. Business Governance
blocks.text_zh: 4.30. 业务治理

blocks.text_en:
Concerned with ensuring that the business processes and policies (and
their operation) deliver the business outcomes and adhere to relevant
business regulation.
blocks.text_zh: 确保业务流程、政策及其运作交付业务结果，遵守相关业务法规。

blocks.text_en: 4.31. Business Model
blocks.text_zh: 4.31. 业务模型

blocks.text_en: A model describing the rationale for how an enterprise creates, delivers, and captures value.
blocks.text_zh: 描述企业如何创造、交付、获取价值的原理的模型。

blocks.text_en: 4.32. Business Service
blocks.text_zh: 4.32. 业务服务

blocks.text_en:
Supports the business by encapsulating a unique “element of business
behavior”.
blocks.text_zh: 封装独特业务行为要素以支持业务。

blocks.text_en:
Note: A service offered external to the enterprise may be supported by
business services.
blocks.text_zh: 注：企业外部服务可由业务服务支撑。

blocks.text_en: 4.33. Capability
An ability that an organization, person, or system possesses.
blocks.text_zh: 组织、人员或系统拥有的能力。

blocks.text_en: Note: This a general-purpose definition. See Section 4.28, “Business Capability” for how this concept is refined for usage in Business Architecture.
blocks.text_zh: 注：通用定义，业务架构细化见4.28业务能力。

blocks.text_en: 4.34. Capability Architecture
blocks.text_zh: 4.34. 能力架构

blocks.text_en: An architecture that describes the abilities that an enterprise possesses.
blocks.text_zh: 描述企业所拥有能力的架构。

blocks.text_en: See also the TOGAF ® Series Guide: A Practitioners’ Approach to Developing Enterprise Architecture Following the TOGAF ADM .
blocks.text_zh: 另见《遵循TOGAF ADM开发企业架构的实践者方法》。

blocks.text_en: 4.35. Capability Increment
blocks.text_zh: 4.35. 能力增量

blocks.text_en:
A discrete portion of a capability architecture that delivers specific
value. When all increments have been completed, the capability has been
realized.
blocks.text_zh: 交付特定价值的能力架构独立部分；全部增量完成时，该能力实现。

blocks.text_en: 4.36. Communications and Stakeholder Management
blocks.text_zh: 4.36. 沟通与利益相关者管理

blocks.text_en:
The management of needs of stakeholders of the Enterprise Architecture
practice. It also manages the execution of communication between the
practice and the stakeholders and the practice and the consumers of its
services.
blocks.text_zh: 管理EA实践利益相关者需要，以及实践与利益相关者、服务消费者之间的沟通执行。

blocks.text_en: Note: Architecture stakeholder management is described in the TOGAF Standard — ADM Techniques .
blocks.text_zh: 注：利益相关者管理见《ADM技术》。

blocks.text_en: 4.37. Concern
An interest in a system relevant to one or more of its stakeholders.
blocks.text_zh: 与一个或多个利益相关者有关的系统利益。

blocks.text_en:
Note: Concerns may pertain to any aspect of the system’s functioning,
development, or operation, including considerations such as
performance, reliability, security, distribution, and evolvability and
may determine the acceptability of the system.
blocks.text_zh: 注：可涉及功能、开发、运营任何方面，如性能、可靠、安全、分布、可演进性，并可能决定系统可接受性。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.76, “Stakeholder” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.76利益相关者。

blocks.text_en: 4.38. Course of Action
blocks.text_zh: 4.38. 行动方案

blocks.text_en: Direction and focus provided by strategic goals and objectives, often to deliver the value proposition characterized in the business model.
blocks.text_zh: 战略目标和具体目标提供的方向及重点，通常用于交付业务模型的价值主张。

blocks.text_en: 4.39. Data Architecture
blocks.text_zh: 4.39. 数据架构

blocks.text_en:
A description of the structure of the enterprise’s major types and
sources of data, logical data assets, physical data assets, and data
management resources.
blocks.text_zh: 描述企业主要数据类型与来源、逻辑及物理数据资产、数据管理资源的结构。

blocks.text_en: Note: Data Architecture is described in the TOGAF Standard — Architecture Method .
blocks.text_zh: 注：本地原文指向《Architecture Method》。

blocks.text_en: 4.40. Deliverable

An architectural work product that is contractually specified and in
turn formally reviewed, agreed, and signed off by the stakeholders.
blocks.text_zh: 契约规定、由利益相关者正式评审商定并签署的架构工作产品。

blocks.text_en:
Note: Deliverables represent the output of projects and those deliverables
that are in documentation form will typically be archived at
completion of a project, or transitioned into an Architecture
Repository as a reference model, standard, or snapshot of the
Architecture Landscape at a point in time.
blocks.text_zh: 注：代表项目输出；文档交付物通常结项归档，或转入储存库作为参考模型、标准、某时点全景快照。

blocks.text_en: 4.41. Digital Architecture
blocks.text_zh: 4.41. 数字架构

blocks.text_en:
The inclusive architecture focused on a combination of Enterprise
Architecture, data science, telecommunications and IoT, security,
artificial intelligence, cognitive science, neuroscience, robotics, and
social medias to deliver operational services.
blocks.text_zh: 结合EA、数据科学、电信与物联网、安全、AI、认知科学、神经科学、机器人、社交媒体，以交付运营服务的包容性架构。

blocks.text_en: 4.42. EA Landscape
blocks.text_zh: 4.42. EA全景

blocks.text_en: See Section 4.15, “Architecture Landscape” .
blocks.text_zh: 见4.15架构全景。

blocks.text_en: 4.43. Enterprise

The highest level (typically) of description of an organization and
typically covers all missions and functions. An enterprise will often
span multiple organizations.
blocks.text_zh: 通常为组织最高层描述，涵盖全部使命和职能，常跨多个组织。

blocks.text_en: 4.44. Enterprise Architecture Service
blocks.text_zh: 4.44. 企业架构服务

blocks.text_en:
An encapsulated element of Enterprise Architecture capability that
delivers specific Enterprise Architecture functionality.
blocks.text_zh: 交付特定EA功能的、经封装的EA能力要素。

blocks.text_en: 4.45. Enterprise Continuum
blocks.text_zh: 4.45. 企业连续系列

blocks.text_en:
A categorization mechanism for classifying architecture and Solution
Building Blocks (SBBs) as they evolve from generic to specific
applicability (or vice versa ).
blocks.text_zh: 对架构及SBB从通用走向特定适用性或反向演进进行分类的机制。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.10, “Architecture Continuum” and Section 4.75, “Solutions Continuum” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.10架构连续系列及4.75解决方案连续系列。

blocks.text_en: 4.46. Foundation Architecture
blocks.text_zh: 4.46. 基础架构

blocks.text_en:
Generic building blocks, their inter-relationships with other building
blocks, combined with the principles and guidelines that provide a
foundation on which more specific architectures can be built.
blocks.text_zh: 通用构建块、相互关系及原则指导的组合，作为构建更特定架构的基础。

blocks.text_en: 4.47. Framework
A structure for content or process that can be used as a tool to structure thinking, ensuring consistency and completeness.
blocks.text_zh: 用于组织思考、确保一致完整的内容或流程结构。

blocks.text_en:
A statement of difference between two states. Used in the context of gap
analysis, where the difference between the Baseline and Target
Architecture is identified.
blocks.text_zh: 两个状态差异的陈述，用于差距分析中识别基线和目标的差异。

blocks.text_en: Note: Gap analysis is described in the TOGAF Standard — ADM Techniques .
blocks.text_zh: 注：见《ADM技术》。

blocks.text_en: 4.49. Governance

The discipline of monitoring and guiding the management of a business
(or IS/IT landscape) to deliver the business outcomes required.
blocks.text_zh: 监控和指导业务或IS/IT全景管理，以交付所需业务结果的纪律。

blocks.text_en:
See also Section 4.14, “Architecture Governance” , Section 4.30, “Business Governance” , Section B.27, “Operational Governance” ,
and Appendix B, Glossary of Supplementary Definitions .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.14架构治理、4.30业务治理、B.27运营治理及附录B。

blocks.text_en: 4.50. Information

Any communication or representation of facts, data, or opinions, in any
medium or form, including textual, numerical, graphic, cartographic, narrative, or audio-visual forms.
blocks.text_zh: 以文字、数字、图形、地图、叙述、视听等任何媒介形式，沟通或表示事实、数据、意见。

blocks.text_en: 4.51. Information Technology (IT)
blocks.text_zh: 4.51. 信息技术IT

blocks.text_en:
The lifecycle management of information and related technology used by
an organization.
blocks.text_zh: 组织所用信息及相关技术的生命周期管理。

blocks.text_en: 4.52. Interoperability
blocks.text_zh: 4.52. 互操作性

blocks.text_en:
The ability to share information and services The ability of two or more systems or components to exchange and use
information The ability of systems to provide and receive services from other
systems and to use the services so interchanged to enable them to
operate effectively together
blocks.text_zh:
1. 共享信息和服务的能力。
2. 两个或多个系统、组件交换并使用信息的能力。
3. 系统相互提供和接收服务，并使用交换服务有效共同运行的能力。

blocks.text_en: 4.53. Logical
Implementation-independent.
blocks.text_zh: 独立于实现。

blocks.text_en:
Note: A logical architecture is an implementation-independent definition of
the architecture.
blocks.text_zh: 注：逻辑架构是实现无关的架构定义。

blocks.text_en: 4.54. Metadata
Data about data, of any sort in any media, that describes the characteristics of an entity.
blocks.text_zh: 任何媒介中的任何类型“关于数据的数据”，描述实体特征。

blocks.text_en: 4.55. Metamodel

A model that describes the entities used in building an Architecture
Description, their characteristics, and the key relationships between
those entities.
blocks.text_zh: 描述构建架构描述所用实体、其特征及关键关系的模型。

blocks.text_en: 4.56. Method
A defined, repeatable approach to address a particular type of problem.
blocks.text_zh: 解决特定问题类型的已定义、可重复途径。

blocks.text_en: 4.57. Modeling

A technique through construction of models which enables a subject to be
represented in a form that enables reasoning, insight, and clarity
concerning the essence of the subject matter.
blocks.text_zh: 通过构建模型，以可推理、洞察和澄清主题本质的形式表示主题的技术。

blocks.text_en: 4.58. Model Kind
blocks.text_zh: 4.58. 模型种类

blocks.text_en: Conventions for a type of modeling.
blocks.text_zh: 一类建模的约定。

blocks.text_en:
Note: An architecture viewpoint references one or more model kinds; an
architecture view incorporates one or more models.
blocks.text_zh: 注：视点引用一个或多个模型种类；视图包含一个或多个模型。

blocks.text_en: 4.59. Objective
blocks.text_zh: 4.59. 具体目标

blocks.text_en:
An organizational aim that is declared in a Specific, Measurable,
Actionable, Realistic, and Timebound (SMART) way. For example, “Increase
capacity utilization by 30% by the end of the year, to support the
planned increase in market share”.
blocks.text_zh: 以具体、可度量、可行动、现实、有时限SMART方式陈述的组织目的，如“年底前容量利用率提高30%，支持计划市场份额增长”。

blocks.text_en: 4.60. Pattern

A technique for putting building blocks into context; for example, to
describe a re-usable solution to a problem.
blocks.text_zh: 将构建块置于语境中的技术，例如描述问题的可复用解决方案。

blocks.text_en:
Note: Building blocks are what you use: (architecture) patterns can tell you
how you use them, when, why, and what trade-offs you have to make in
doing so.
blocks.text_zh: 注：构建块是用什么，模式可说明如何、何时、为何使用及相应取舍。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.26, “Building Block” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.26构建块。

blocks.text_en: 4.61. Physical
Real-world, tangible.
blocks.text_zh: 现实世界、可触及的。

blocks.text_en: Note: A logical architecture is realized through a physical architecture.
blocks.text_zh: 注：逻辑架构通过物理架构实现。

blocks.text_en: 4.62. Principle
See Section 4.19, “Architecture Principle” .
blocks.text_zh: 见4.19架构原则。

blocks.text_en: 4.63. Product
An outcome generated by the business to be offered to customers. Products include materials and/or services.
blocks.text_zh: 业务产生、提供给客户的结果，包括材料和/或服务。

blocks.text_en: 4.64. Reference Model (RM)
blocks.text_zh: 4.64. 参考模型RM

blocks.text_en:
An abstract framework for understanding significant relationships among
the entities of [an] environment, and for the development of consistent
standards or specifications supporting that environment.
blocks.text_zh: 用于理解环境实体的重要关系，并开发支持环境的一致标准或规格的抽象框架。

blocks.text_en:
Note: A reference model is based on a small number of unifying concepts and
may be used as a basis for education and explaining standards to a
non-specialist. A reference model is not directly tied to any
standards, technologies, or other concrete implementation details, but
it does seek to provide common semantics that can be used
unambiguously across and between different implementations. Source: OASIS ® ; refer to www.oasis-open.org/committees/soa-rm/faq.php .
blocks.text_zh: 注：基于少量统一概念，可用于教育、向非专家讲解标准；不直接绑定标准、技术或具体实现，而寻求跨实现无歧义的共同语义。来源OASIS：www.oasis-open.org/committees/soa-rm/faq.php。

blocks.text_en: 4.65. Requirement

A statement of need, which is unambiguous, testable or measurable, and
necessary for acceptability.
blocks.text_zh: 无歧义、可测试或度量，且是可接受性必要条件的需要陈述。

blocks.text_en: 4.66. Roadmap

An abstracted plan for business or technology change, typically
operating across multiple disciplines over multiple years. Normally used
in the phrases Technology Roadmap, Architecture Roadmap, etc.
blocks.text_zh: 业务或技术变革的抽象计划，通常跨学科、跨多年，常见于技术路线图、架构路线图等用语。

blocks.text_en: 4.67. Role

The usual or expected behavior of an actor, or the part somebody or something plays in a particular process or event. An actor may have a number of roles The part an individual plays in an organization and the contribution they make through the application of their skills, knowledge,
experience, and abilities
blocks.text_zh:
1. 参与者通常或预期的行为，或某人、某物在流程事件中的作用；一个参与者可有多个角色。
2. 个人在组织中所起作用，以及应用技能、知识、经验和能力作出的贡献。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.2, “Actor” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.2参与者。

blocks.text_en: 4.68. Segment Architecture
blocks.text_zh: 4.68. 分段架构

blocks.text_en: A detailed, formal description of areas within an enterprise, used at the program or portfolio level to organize and align change activity.
blocks.text_zh: 企业内某领域的详细正式描述，用于项目群或组合层组织、对齐变革活动。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.78, “Strategic Architecture” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.78战略架构。

blocks.text_en: 4.69. Service

An encapsulated element of behavior that provides specific functionality
in response to requests from actors or other services.
blocks.text_zh: 响应参与者或其他服务请求、提供特定功能的封装行为要素。

blocks.text_en: Note: A service has an interface and description.
blocks.text_zh: 注：服务有接口和描述。

blocks.text_en: 4.70. Service Orientation
blocks.text_zh: 4.70. 服务导向

blocks.text_en:
Viewing an enterprise, system, or building block in terms of services
provided and consumed.
blocks.text_zh: 以提供和消费的服务看待企业、系统或构建块。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.71, “Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA)” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.71面向服务架构。

blocks.text_en: 4.71. Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA)
blocks.text_zh: 4.71. 面向服务架构SOA

blocks.text_en: An architectural style that supports service orientation.
blocks.text_zh: 支持服务导向的架构风格。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.7, “Architectural Style” and Section 4.70, “Service Orientation” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.7架构风格、4.70服务导向。

blocks.text_en: 4.72. Service Portfolio
blocks.text_zh: 4.72. 服务组合

blocks.text_en: A collection of services, potentially an interface definition.
blocks.text_zh: 服务集合，可能是接口定义。

blocks.text_en: Note: It is used in the TOGAF framework to define the requirement for a building block or system.
blocks.text_zh: 注：在TOGAF中用于定义构建块或系统需求。

blocks.text_en: 4.73. Solution Architecture
blocks.text_zh: 4.73. 解决方案架构

blocks.text_en: A description of a discrete and focused business operation or activity and how IS/IT supports that operation.
blocks.text_zh: 描述一项离散聚焦的业务运营或活动，以及IS/IT如何支持它。

blocks.text_en: 4.74. Solution Building Block (SBB)
blocks.text_zh: 4.74. 解决方案构建块SBB

blocks.text_en: A physical or implementation-specific component that realizes part or all of one or more logical Architecture Building Blocks (ABBs).
blocks.text_zh: 实现一个或多个逻辑ABB部分或全部的物理或实施特定组件。

blocks.text_en: Note: There are business, application, and technology SBBs.
blocks.text_zh: 注：有业务、应用、技术SBB。

blocks.text_en: 4.75. Solutions Continuum
blocks.text_zh: 4.75. 解决方案连续系列

blocks.text_en: A categorization mechanism, with increasing detail and specialization, for the components and artifacts stored in the Solutions Landscape or Reference Library (part of the Architecture Repository).
blocks.text_zh: 按不断增加的细节和特化程度，对解决方案全景或参考库（储存库一部分）内组件制品分类的机制。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.45, “Enterprise Continuum” and Section 4.10, “Architecture Continuum” .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.45企业连续系列、4.10架构连续系列。

blocks.text_en: 4.76. Stakeholder
blocks.text_zh: 4.76. 利益相关者

blocks.text_en:
An individual, team, organization, or class thereof, having an interest
in a system.
blocks.text_zh: 对系统有利益关联的个人、团队、组织或其类别。

blocks.text_en: 4.77. Standards Library

A library of standards that can be used to define the particular
services and other components of an Organization-Specific Architecture.
blocks.text_zh: 可用于定义组织特定架构的特定服务及其他组件的标准库。

blocks.text_en: Note: The Standards Library is described in the TOGAF Standard — Architecture Content .
blocks.text_zh: 注：见《架构内容》。

blocks.text_en: 4.78. Strategic Architecture
blocks.text_zh: 4.78. 战略架构

blocks.text_en: A summary formal description of the enterprise, providing an organizing framework for operational and change activity, and an executive-level, long-term view for direction setting.
blocks.text_zh: 企业的概要正式描述，提供组织运营和变革活动的框架，以及用于方向设定的高管级长期视图。

blocks.text_en: 4.79. Target Architecture
blocks.text_zh: 4.79. 目标架构

blocks.text_en:
The description of a future state of the architecture being developed
for an organization.
blocks.text_zh: 为组织开发的架构未来状态描述。

blocks.text_en: Note: There may be several future states developed as a roadmap to show the evolution of the architecture to a target state.
blocks.text_zh: 注：可有多个未来状态，作为路线图展示向目标演进。

blocks.text_en: 4.80. Taxonomy of Architecture Views
blocks.text_zh: 4.80. 架构视图分类体系

blocks.text_en:
The organized collection of all architecture views pertinent to an
architecture.
blocks.text_zh: 与架构有关的全部视图的有序集合。

blocks.text_en: 4.81. Technology Architecture
blocks.text_zh: 4.81. 技术架构

blocks.text_en:
A description of the structure and interaction of the technology
services and technology components.
blocks.text_zh: 描述技术服务和组件的结构与交互。

blocks.text_en: Note: Technology Architecture is described in the TOGAF Standard — Architecture Development Method .
blocks.text_zh: 注：见《架构开发方法》。

blocks.text_en: 4.82. Technology Component
blocks.text_zh: 4.82. 技术组件

blocks.text_en:
A technology building block. A generic infrastructure technology that
supports and enables application or data components (directly or indirectly) by providing technology services An encapsulation of technology infrastructure that represents a class of technology product or specific technology product
blocks.text_zh:
1. 技术构建块：提供技术服务，直接或间接使能、支持应用或数据组件的通用基础设施技术。
2. 代表某类或特定技术产品的基础设施封装。

blocks.text_en: 4.83. Technology Service
blocks.text_zh: 4.83. 技术服务

blocks.text_en: A technical capability required to provide enabling infrastructure that supports the delivery of applications.
blocks.text_zh: 提供使能基础设施、支持应用交付所需的技术能力。

blocks.text_en: 4.84. Transition Architecture
blocks.text_zh: 4.84. 过渡架构

blocks.text_en:
A formal description of one state of the architecture at an
architecturally significant point in time.
blocks.text_zh: 在具有架构意义的时点，对一个架构状态的正式描述。

blocks.text_en: Note: One or more Transition Architectures may be used to describe the progression in time from the Baseline to the Target Architecture. Transition Architecture is described in the TOGAF Standard — Architecture Content .
blocks.text_zh: 注：一个或多个过渡架构可描述从基线到目标的时间推进，详见《架构内容》。

blocks.text_en: 4.85. Value Stream

A representation of an end-to-end collection of activities that create
an overall result for a customer, stakeholder, or end user.
blocks.text_zh: 为客户、利益相关者或最终用户创造整体结果的端到端活动集合的表示。

blocks.text_en: 4.86. View
See Section 4.20, “Architecture View” .
blocks.text_zh: 见4.20架构视图。

blocks.text_en: 4.87. Viewpoint
See Section 4.21, “Architecture Viewpoint” .
blocks.text_zh: 见4.21架构视点。

blocks.text_en: 4.88. Viewpoint Library

A collection of the specifications of architecture viewpoints contained
in the Reference Library portion of the Architecture Repository.
blocks.text_zh: 储存库参考库中保存的视点规格集合。

blocks.text_en: 4.89. Work Package

A set of actions identified to achieve one or more objectives for the
business. A work package can be a part of a project, a complete project,
or a program.
blocks.text_zh: 为实现一个或多个业务具体目标而识别的行动集合，可为项目一部分、完整项目或项目群。

blocks.text_en: B: Glossary of Supplementary Definitions
blocks.text_zh: B：补充定义词汇表

blocks.text_en:
This appendix contains additional definitions to supplement the
definitions contained in Chapter 4, Definitions .
blocks.text_zh: 本附录补充第4章定义。

blocks.text_en: B.1. Application Software
blocks.text_zh: B.1. 应用软件

blocks.text_en: Software entities which have a specific business purpose.
blocks.text_zh: 具有特定业务目的的软件实体。

blocks.text_en: B.2. Availability
blocks.text_zh: B.2. 可用性

blocks.text_en:
In the context of IT systems, the probability that system functional
capabilities are ready for use by a user at any time, where all time is
considered, including operations, repair, administration, and logistic
time. Availability is further defined by system category for both
routine and priority operations.
blocks.text_zh: IT系统中，用户在任意时点可使用系统功能的概率，考虑运营、修复、管理及后勤等全部时间；按系统类别进一步定义常规及优先操作可用性。

blocks.text_en: B.3. Business System
blocks.text_zh: B.3. 业务系统

blocks.text_en:
Hardware, software, policy statements, processes, activities, standards,
and people which together implement a business capability.
blocks.text_zh: 共同实现业务能力的硬件、软件、政策声明、流程、活动、标准和人员。

blocks.text_en: B.4. Catalog
blocks.text_zh: B.4. 目录

blocks.text_en:
A structured list of architectural outputs of a similar kind, used for
reference. For example, a technology standards catalog or an application
portfolio.
blocks.text_zh: 用于参考的同类架构输出结构化清单，如技术标准目录或应用组合。

blocks.text_en: B.5. Client
blocks.text_zh: B.5. 客户端

blocks.text_en: An application component which requests services from a server.
blocks.text_zh: 向服务器请求服务的应用组件。

blocks.text_en: B.6. COBIT
blocks.text_zh: B.6. COBIT控制目标

blocks.text_en:
An acronym for Control OBjectives for Information and related
Technology, created by the Information Systems Audit and Control
Association (ISACA) and the IT Governance Institute (ITGI), which
provides a set of recommended best practices for the
governance/management of information systems and technology.
blocks.text_zh: “信息及相关技术控制目标”的缩写，由ISACA及ITGI创建，为信息系统与技术治理/管理提供最佳实践建议。

blocks.text_en: B.7. Configuration Management
blocks.text_zh: B.7. 配置管理

blocks.text_en:
A discipline applying technical and administrative direction and
surveillance to:
blocks.text_zh: 以技术和行政指导及监督开展以下工作的纪律：

blocks.text_en:
Identify and document the functional and physical characteristics of a
configuration item Control changes to those characteristics Record and report changes to processing and implementation status
blocks.text_zh:
- 识别并记录配置项功能及物理特征。
- 控制特征变更。
- 记录报告处理及实施状态变化。

blocks.text_en:
Also, the management of the configuration of Enterprise Architecture
practice (intellectual property) assets and baselines and the control of
change over of those assets.
blocks.text_zh: 也指管理EA实践知识产权资产和基线配置，并控制其变更。

blocks.text_en: B.8. CxO
blocks.text_zh: B.8. CxO高管

blocks.text_en:
The chief officer within a particular function of the business; e.g.,
Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Information
Officer, Chief Technology Officer.
blocks.text_zh: 特定业务职能最高负责人，如CEO、CFO、CIO、CTO。

blocks.text_en: B.9. Data Dictionary
blocks.text_zh: B.9. 数据字典

blocks.text_en:
A specialized type of database containing metadata; a repository of
information describing the characteristics of data used to design,
monitor, document, protect, and control data in information systems and
databases; an application system supporting the definition and
management of database metadata.
blocks.text_zh: 含元数据的专门数据库；保存数据特征信息，用于设计、监控、记录、保护和控制信息系统及数据库数据；支持元数据定义管理的应用系统。

blocks.text_en: B.10. Data Element
blocks.text_zh: B.10. 数据元素

blocks.text_en:
A basic unit of information having a meaning and that may have
subcategories (data items) of distinct units and values.
blocks.text_zh: 具有意义的信息基本单位，可包含有独立单位和值的数据项子类。

blocks.text_en: B.11. Database
blocks.text_zh: B.11. 数据库

blocks.text_en:
A structured or organized collection of data entities, which is to be
accessed by a computer.
blocks.text_zh: 供计算机访问的、结构化或有组织的数据实体集合。

blocks.text_en: B.12. Database Management System
blocks.text_zh: B.12. 数据库管理系统

blocks.text_en:
A computer application program that accesses or manipulates the
database.
blocks.text_zh: 访问或操作数据库的计算机应用程序。

blocks.text_en: B.13. End User
blocks.text_zh: B.13. 最终用户

blocks.text_en: Person who ultimately uses the computer application or output.
blocks.text_zh: 最终使用计算机应用或输出的人。

blocks.text_en: B.14. Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) System
blocks.text_zh: B.14. 企业资源规划ERP系统

blocks.text_en:
A complete suite of integrated applications that support the major
business support functions of an organization; e.g., Financial
(AP/AR/GL), HR, Payroll, Stock, Order Processing and Invoicing,
Purchasing, Logistics, Manufacturing, etc.
blocks.text_zh: 支持主要业务支撑职能的完整集成应用套件，例如财务（应付、应收、总账）、人力、薪资、库存、订单及开票、采购、物流、制造等。

blocks.text_en: B.15. Hardware
blocks.text_zh: B.15. 硬件

blocks.text_en:
The physical infrastructure needed to run software; e.g., servers,
workstations, network equipment, etc.
blocks.text_zh: 运行软件所需物理基础设施，如服务器、工作站、网络设备。

blocks.text_en: B.16. Information Domain
blocks.text_zh: B.16. 信息域

blocks.text_en:
Grouping of information (or data entities) by a set of criteria such as
security classification, ownership, location, etc. In the context of
security, information domains are defined as a set of users, their
information objects, and a security policy.
blocks.text_zh: 按安全分类、所有权、位置等准则分组的信息或实体。安全语境中指一组用户、其信息对象和安全政策。

blocks.text_en: B.17. Information System (IS)
blocks.text_zh: B.17. 信息系统IS

blocks.text_en: The computer (or IT)-based portion of a business system.
blocks.text_zh: 业务系统中基于计算机或IT的部分。

blocks.text_en: B.18. Interaction
blocks.text_zh: B.18. 交互

blocks.text_en:
A relationship between architectural building blocks (i.e., services or
components) that embodies communication or usage.
blocks.text_zh: 体现通信或使用的架构构建块（服务或组件）关系。

blocks.text_en: B.19. Interaction Model
blocks.text_zh: B.19. 交互模型

blocks.text_en:
An architectural view, catalog, or matrix that shows a particular type
of interaction. For example, a diagram showing application integration.
blocks.text_zh: 展示特定交互类型的视图、目录或矩阵，例如应用集成图。

blocks.text_en: B.20. Interface
blocks.text_zh: B.20. 接口

blocks.text_en:
Interconnection and inter-relationships between, for example, people,
systems, devices, applications, or the user and an application or
device.
blocks.text_zh: 人与人、系统、设备、应用，或用户与应用/设备之间的互连及相互关系。

blocks.text_en: B.21. Key Performance Indicator (KPI)
blocks.text_zh: B.21. 关键绩效指标KPI

blocks.text_en: A way of quantifying the performance of the business or project.
blocks.text_zh: 量化业务或项目绩效的方式。

blocks.text_en: B.22. Lifecycle
blocks.text_zh: B.22. 生命周期

blocks.text_en:
The period of time that begins when a system is conceived and ends when
the system is no longer available for use.
blocks.text_zh: 从系统构思开始到不再可用结束的时间段。

blocks.text_en: B.23. Managing Successful Programs (MSP)
blocks.text_zh: B.23. 成功项目群管理MSP

blocks.text_en:
A best practice methodology for program management, developed by the UK
Office of Government Commerce (OGC).
blocks.text_zh: 英国政府商务办公室OGC开发的项目群管理最佳实践方法。

blocks.text_en: B.24. Matrix
blocks.text_zh: B.24. 矩阵

blocks.text_en:
A format for showing the relationship between two (or more)
architectural elements in a grid format.
blocks.text_zh: 以网格展示两个或多个架构要素关系的形式。

blocks.text_en: B.25. Metaview
blocks.text_zh: B.25. 元视图

blocks.text_en:
A pattern or template of the view, from which to develop individual
views. Establishes the purposes and audience for a view, the ways in
which the view is documented (e.g., for visual modeling), and the ways
in which it is used (e.g., for analysis).
blocks.text_zh: 用于开发个别视图的模式或模板，确立目的、受众、记录方式（如可视建模）及使用方式（如分析）。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.21, “Architecture Viewpoint” in Chapter 4, Definitions .
blocks.text_zh: 另见第4章4.21架构视点。

blocks.text_en: B.26. Open System
blocks.text_zh: B.26. 开放系统

blocks.text_en:
A system that implements sufficient open specifications for interfaces,
services, and supporting formats to enable properly engineered
application software:
blocks.text_zh: 实现足够开放的接口、服务和支撑格式规格，使正确工程化的应用软件能够：

blocks.text_en: To be ported with minimal changes across a wide range of systems To interoperate with other applications on local and remote systems To interact with users in a style that facilitates user portability
blocks.text_zh:
- 在广泛系统间以最小改动移植。
- 与本地、远程应用互操作。
- 以有利于用户迁移的方式交互。

blocks.text_en: B.27. Operational Governance
blocks.text_zh: B.27. 运营治理

blocks.text_en:
The operational performance of systems against contracted performance
levels, the definition of operational performance levels, and the
implementation of systems that ensure effective operation of systems.
blocks.text_zh: 按契约绩效水平管理系统运营表现、定义运营水平并实施确保有效运行的系统。

blocks.text_en: See also Section 4.49, “Governance” in Chapter 4, Definitions .
blocks.text_zh: 另见4.49治理。

blocks.text_en: B.28. Packaged Services
blocks.text_zh: B.28. 套装服务

blocks.text_en:
Services that are acquired from the market from a Commercial
Off-The-Shelf (COTS) vendor, rather than being constructed via code
build.
blocks.text_zh: 从COTS供应商市场采购、而非编码自建的服务。

blocks.text_en: B.29. Portability
blocks.text_zh: B.29. 可迁移性

blocks.text_en:
The ease with which a system, component, data, or user can be
transferred from one hardware or software environment to another A quality metric that can be used to measure the relative effort to
transport the software for use in another environment or to convert
software for use in another operating environment, hardware
configuration, or software system environment
blocks.text_zh:
1. 系统、组件、数据或用户在软硬件环境间转移的容易程度。
2. 衡量将软件迁至另一环境，或转换至另一操作环境、硬件配置、软件系统环境所需相对工作量的质量指标。

blocks.text_en: B.30. Portfolio
blocks.text_zh: B.30. 组合

blocks.text_en:
A collection of programs, projects, and/or operations managed as a group to achieve strategic objectives. For example, project portfolio,
application portfolio, technology portfolio, or service portfolio.
blocks.text_zh: 为实现战略具体目标而作为一组管理的项目群、项目和/或运营集合，如项目、应用、技术或服务组合。

blocks.text_en: Note: Portfolio management is the act of managing portfolios.
blocks.text_zh: 注：组合管理即管理组合的行为。

blocks.text_en: B.31. PRINCE2
blocks.text_zh: B.31. PRINCE2方法

blocks.text_en:
An acronym for PRojects IN Controlled Environments, which is a standard
project management method.
blocks.text_zh: “受控环境中的项目”的缩写，是标准项目管理方法。

blocks.text_en: B.32. Program
blocks.text_zh: B.32. 项目群

blocks.text_en:
A co-ordinated set of change projects that deliver business benefit to
the organization.
blocks.text_zh: 向组织交付业务收益的、经协调的变革项目集合。

blocks.text_en: B.33. Project
blocks.text_zh: B.33. 项目

blocks.text_en:
A single change project which delivers business benefit to the
organization.
blocks.text_zh: 向组织交付业务收益的单个变革项目。

blocks.text_en: B.34. Risk Management
blocks.text_zh: B.34. 风险管理

blocks.text_en:
The management of risks and issues that may threaten the success of the
Enterprise Architecture practice and its ability to meet its vision,
goals, and objectives, and, importantly, its service provision.
blocks.text_zh: 管理可能威胁EA实践成功、愿景、目标及具体目标实现、尤其服务提供的风险和问题。

blocks.text_en: Note: Risk management is described in the TOGAF Standard — Architecture Content .
blocks.text_zh: 注：本地原文指向《架构内容》。

blocks.text_en: B.35. Scalability
blocks.text_zh: B.35. 可伸缩性

blocks.text_en:
The ability to use the same application software on many different
classes of hardware/software platforms from PCs to super-computers
(extends the portability concept). The capability to grow to accommodate
increased work loads.
blocks.text_zh: 同一应用用于PC到超级计算机等不同软硬件平台的能力，扩展可迁移概念；以及增长以承载增加负载的能力。

blocks.text_en: B.36. Security
blocks.text_zh: B.36. 安全

blocks.text_en:
Services which protect data, ensuring its confidentiality, availability,
and integrity.
blocks.text_zh: 保护数据、确保机密性、可用性和完整性的服务。

blocks.text_en: B.37. Server
blocks.text_zh: B.37. 服务器

blocks.text_en: An application component which responds to requests from a client.
blocks.text_zh: 响应客户端请求的应用组件。

blocks.text_en: B.38. Service Quality
blocks.text_zh: B.38. 服务质量

blocks.text_en:
A preset configuration of non-functional attributes that may be assigned
to a service or service contract.
blocks.text_zh: 可分配给服务或契约的非功能属性预设配置。

blocks.text_en: B.39. SMART
blocks.text_zh: B.39. SMART准则

blocks.text_en:
An acronym for Specific, Measurable, Actionable, Realistic, and
Timebound, which is an approach to ensure that targets and objectives
are set in a way that can be achieved and measured.
blocks.text_zh: 具体、可度量、可行动、现实、有时限的缩写，用于确保目标和具体目标可实现、可测量。

blocks.text_en: B.40. Supplier Management
blocks.text_zh: B.40. 供应商管理

blocks.text_en:
The management of suppliers of products and services to the Enterprise
Architecture practice in concert with larger corporate procurement
activities.
blocks.text_zh: 配合公司整体采购，管理向EA实践提供产品和服务的供应商。

blocks.text_en: B.41. System
blocks.text_zh: B.41. 系统

blocks.text_en:
A combination of interacting elements organized to achieve one or more
stated purposes. (Source: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2015)
blocks.text_zh: 为实现一个或多个规定目的而组织的交互要素组合，来源ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2015。

blocks.text_en: B.42. Time Period
blocks.text_zh: B.42. 时间段

blocks.text_en: The timeframe over which the potential impact is to be measured.
blocks.text_zh: 测量潜在影响的时间跨度。

blocks.text_en: B.43. Use Case
blocks.text_zh: B.43. 用例

blocks.text_en:
A view of organization, application, or product functionality that
illustrates capabilities in context with the user of that capability.
blocks.text_zh: 将能力置于使用者语境、展示组织、应用或产品功能的视图。

blocks.text_en: B.44. User
blocks.text_zh: B.44. 用户

blocks.text_en:
Any person, organization, or functional unit that uses the services of
an information processing system In a conceptual schema language, any person or any thing that may
issue or receive commands and messages to or from the information
system
blocks.text_zh:
1. 使用信息处理系统服务的个人、组织或职能单元。
2. 概念模式语言中，可能向系统发出或接收命令消息的任何人或事物。
